extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Art of Computer Programming and people who report errata or submit text amendments to TAOCP Volume 3 (contributors, editors, and conscientious readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and conventions used by Donald Knuth for classifying, formatting, and publishing corrections, amendments, improvements, and plans for Volume 3 (Sorting and Searching) errata. Includes how to report suggestions and which changes appear in hardcopy vs long-form listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levels of updates (bugonpage / amendpage / improvepage / planforpage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three levels of changes to the books are distinguished here: "\bugonpage" introduces the correction of an error; "\amendpage" introduces new material for future editions; "\improvepage" introduces ameliorations of lesser importance. Also, "\planforpage" introduces some of the author's half-baked intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are indicated by distinct typographic conventions. (Note: depending on the inclusion flag, four levels may be shown; improvements may be omitted from the hardcopy listing.)

rubrics_metrics.name: bugonpage (technical or typographical errors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical or typographical errors (aka bugs) are the most critical items, so they are flagged with a `\thinspace{\manfnt x}\thinspace' preceding the page number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date shown for a bug is the effective date on which the author first was told about the bug (and when the finder's fee was paid). Necessary corrections are indicated straightforwardly; e.g., if the book says `n' where it should have said `n+1', the change is shown thus: `n \becomes n+1'.

rubrics_metrics.name: amendpage (amendments to the text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the text appear in the same format as bugs, but without the `\thinspace{\manfnt x}\thinspace'. These are things the author wishes he had known about or thought of when he wrote the original text, so he added them later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date shown for an amendment is the date the author drafted the new text.

rubrics_metrics.name: planforpage (plans for the future)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for the future represent a kind of item in which the author sketches intentions that he was not ready to flesh out. You can identify these items because they're written in slanted type and preceded by a bunch of dots leading to the date on which the plan was recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans are explicitly marked typographically (slanted + dot leader to date) to distinguish them from corrections and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: improvepage (minor improvements / trivial corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fourth category consists of minor corrections or improvements that most readers don't want to know about, because they are so trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are indicated by page and line number in smaller, slanted type; changes introduced by \improvepage do not appear in the hardcopy listing unless the full (long) form of the errata is requested. The document offers an inclusion flag (\alltrue) to show these trivial items if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic conventions for marking entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Different kinds of entries are distinguished by typographic signals: a black triangle (`\manfnt x') for bugs, slanted type and dot leaders for plans, smaller slanted type for improvements, and normal bold page-number lines for amendments and other entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry also shows page and line reference (e.g., "Page 3.93") and a date in the entry header. Corrections are shown using the `\becomes' notation to indicate 'before \becomes after'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date semantics for errata entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates shown in entries have meanings tied to the kind of item: for bugs the date is when the author was first told about the bug (effective date for finder's fee); for amendments the date is when the new text was drafted; plan dates are when the plan was recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date format is shown in yy.mm.dd. and converted to a verbose form in the listing. The finder's-fee date is important for the bug category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of corrections (use of \becomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary corrections are indicated in a straightforward way using the `\becomes' notation to show the original text and the corrected text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: `n \becomes n+1'. Replacement lines and block replacements are shown similarly, and entire lines or program fragments can be replaced as shown in the errata entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion flag for trivial items (\ifall / \alltrue)
rubrics_metrics.description: A flag (\ifall / \alltrue) controls whether trivial items (improvements) are shown. `\alltrue' means show the trivial items too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the flag is not set, minor improvements are omitted from the short/hardcopy errata listing; the long form or the full list online contains them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Volume 3 being considered 'up to date'
rubrics_metrics.description: The author believes the changes listed bring Volume 3 completely up to date in two respects: (1) All research problems in the previous edition (exercises rated 46 and above) have received new ratings of 45 or less whenever he learned of a solution, and in such cases, the answer now refers to that solution. (2) All of the historical information about pioneering developments has been amended whenever new details have come to his attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This states the substantive standards by which the author judges the volume current: solutions discovered for high-rated exercises and corrected historical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and address for reporting suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Send your comments either by snail mail to D. E. Knuth, Computer Science, Gates Building 4B, Stanford University, Stanford CA 94305-9045, or by email to taocp@cs.stanford.edu. (Use email for book suggestions only, please---all other correspondence is returned unread to the sender, or discarded.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author asks that email be used only for book suggestions; other correspondence via email will be ignored. He will try to reply to such messages within a year of receipt. Current news and the full (long) errata list are available on the TAOCP website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and distinction of long-form errata
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'long form' of the errata exists (full list) that includes the 'gory details' and the trivial improvements not shown in the short/hardcopy listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To see everything, download the full list from the TAOCP webpage by selecting the 'long form' of the errata; the printed short list omits the trivial \improvepage items unless the inclusion flag is set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index-change reporting policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Miscellaneous changes to the existing index of Volume 3 are collected, including corrections and amendments to old entries as well as new entries occasioned by new material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a correction or amendment has caused an old index entry to be deleted, the deletion is usually not indicated. The lines of the full index that have changed serve also as an index to the errata document.
